The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T15:54:00Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-12T15:54:03Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came 6 minutes {detection_gap} after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
Broken from 2026-11-12T15:47:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-12T15:58:39Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 11 minutes 39 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 4 minutes 37 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T15:58:39Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 31.2% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 42.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 30.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9000000000000001% {series_before} before it began, 31.20833333333333% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 42.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 8,265.67 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-12T15:47:53Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - [P2] 2026-11-12T15:54:14Z {P2.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by Argus: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched off
  - [P3] 2026-11-12T15:57:03Z {P3.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by Argus: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 15:17–15:46 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 41 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 36 {G46bc.2} minutes, 15:17–15:52 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 35 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 38 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 15:17–15:54 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 42.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 15:54 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 3 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 13 {Gad41.2} minutes, 15:26–15:38 {Gad41.3}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 184 {G971b.1} / on 16 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 15:47 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 15 {G5309.1} occurrences in 8 {G5309.2} minutes, 15:47–15:54 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 7 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 7 {Gce95.3} minutes, 15:48–15:54 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of monthly-spend-feature, each in its own words:
      C1: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-12T15:47:53Z {C1.1}. This enabled a spend summary code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and account page requests started failing. The error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to 30-40% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, refuted]
      C2: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-12T15:47:53Z {C1.5}. This enabled the spend summary code path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the account page error rate rose from about 1% {C1.6} to 30-40% {C1.7}. Argus's own switch-off at 2026-11-12T15:54:14Z {C1.8} did not help, and Argus switched the flag back on at 2026-11-12T15:57:03Z {C1.9}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.85 {C1.10}, refuted, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` returned `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`. It divides by however many purchases are flagged `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has zero of those, so the function raised ZeroDivisionError. The incident evidence places that error at line 47 {F1.1}. The test file calls this kind of shopper "the ordinary case". `render_spend_summary` sends the request to this function when `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false, which is the path monthly-spend-feature turns on.
      
      The change: if nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0 {F1.2}, meaning no spend per item this month. Otherwise it divides as before. The return type stays `int`.
      
      Nothing is being silenced. No exception is caught; the empty month just gets the answer it should have. The lifetime figure, the typical-spend figure and the flag-off path in this file are untouched. That includes the existing test where a shopper with no history at all still raises through `render_spend_summary` with the flag off.
      
      Tests added to tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py:
      - One calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` for a shopper with past purchases but none this month and expects 0 {F1.3}. Against the old code this test would raise ZeroDivisionError.
      - One calls `render_spend_summary` with `use_monthly_summary=True` for the same kind of shopper and expects 0 {F1.4}. It covers the path the flag turns on.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #575 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` sends the account page request to `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month that number is zero, so the request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the account page fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Account pages started failing when a setting switched on a new monthly spending summary, and that summary likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.
still_at_risk: Account page requests could go on failing with the division-by-zero error at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 while monthly-spend-feature stays on, and it was left on.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed
stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop that its flag evaluation log lines read off for every evaluation and that the ZeroDivisionError lines at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 stop.
why_it_did_not_help: Find out from io-shop's flag evaluation log lines after the switch-off whether the service read monthly-spend-feature as off. If it did, find out what else kept reaching the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and kept the account pages failing.
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of failed account page requests in the minute rose far above its usual level. (cites AL1; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors started in the minute of the onset and were not seen before it. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations went from all off to all on starting in that minute, so account page requests began running the spend summary code path that the flag turns on. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: The service with the flag off: before the onset every evaluation read off, account pages rendered normally, and the error rate was typically low. (cites G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: Shoppers closing the connection: these ClientDisconnected failures were already being logged during the healthy stretch before the onset, while the error rate stayed typically low. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: The spend summary path divides by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every evaluation at once. No staged rollout to a small share of traffic was seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account page requests would have taken the failing path, and the errors could have been caught before the flag reached all traffic.
contributing_factors 2: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the code path it turns on for a shopper with past purchases but none this month.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have shown up before the flag went on, and the flag would not have been switched on with the path failing.
contributing_factors 3: Nobody was paged: HighErrorRate on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been working the incident from the alert onward, including after the flag revert did not help, rather than only when a draft pull request was left for review.
action_items 1: Make flag changes on io-shop roll out to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the account page error rate stays at its usual level.
action_items 2: Require a test that runs the code path an io-shop flag turns on, including for shoppers with no purchases this month, and have it pass before the flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 3: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call engineer.
went_wrong 1: Switching off the flag that the onset lines up with did not take the service off the incident's level. That left the incident with no mitigation, and the service was still failing when Argus escalated.
went_wrong 2: The second investigation formed C2, which blames the same flag move that had just been tested and refuted, so it offered nothing new to try.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
